assemblies.name: Batch Carriage Build â€” All 4 Axes
assemblies.description: Builds all four axis carriages in one production-line session before individual axis bench work begins. Lays out all eight carriage halves at once, then assembles each carriage sequentially: seat bearings, run shake and rod-slide tests, close halves, bolt and tighten. Produces four completed carriages â€” Y-Left, Y-Right, Z-Back, and Z-Front â€” ready to be threaded onto guide rods during per-axis bench builds.
assemblies.learningFocus: Production-line carriage assembly: seat four LM8UU bearings per carriage with flanges out, verify fit with shake and rod-slide tests before closing, align belt holes correctly before bolting, and build all four carriages in one session to establish muscle memory before individual axis bench work.

partGroups.name: All Axis Carriages â€” Batch Build
partGroups.description: Batch assembly of all four axis carriages: Y-Left, Y-Right, Z-Back, and Z-Front. All eight carriage halves are laid out together. Each carriage is built sequentially using the same procedure: seat four LM8UU bearings with flanges facing out, shake test, rod-slide test, close halves, insert M6x18 (top) and M6x30 (bottom) bolts, tighten with power drill. Z-Back and Z-Front use a combined-half carriage model.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: All four axis carriages assembled: bearings seated, belt holes aligned, halves bolted. Ready for individual axis bench builds.

guidance.instructionText: Gather and lay out all six carriage pieces on the workbench: Y-Left half A, Y-Left half B, Y-Right half A, Y-Right half B, Z-Back carriage (single piece), Z-Front carriage (single piece). Also set out the hardware for each Y-axis carriage: M6Ã—18 bolts (top holes), M6Ã—30 bolts (bottom holes), and M6 nuts.
guidance.whyItMattersText: Building all four carriages in one session creates muscle memory for the bearing-seating technique before moving to individual axis builds. Laying everything out first lets you spot missing parts before work begins.

steps.name: Clean excess plastic from all carriage holes
steps.instructionText: Use a box cutter or cordless power drill to clear excess plastic from all semi-circle rod holes in each carriage half-piece. Work through all 8 halves before moving on. Holes must be smooth so bearings seat fully and rods insert freely.

steps.name: QC: verify all carriage holes are clean
steps.instructionText: Check every carriage half: each half should have 4 clean semi-circle rod holes, and the M6 bolt holes must be clear of excess plastic. Run a bolt through each hole by hand to confirm clearance before starting the bearing assembly.

steps.name: Carriage 1 (Y-Left): place 4 LM8UU bearings
steps.instructionText: Place four LM8UU linear bearings into one Y-Left carriage half-piece. Flanges must face outward â€” away from each other â€” so they sit flush in the lip of each pocket.

steps.name: Carriage 1: close the second carriage half
steps.instructionText: Place the second Y-Left carriage half onto the first, trapping the 4 bearings in their pockets. The small ribbed belt hole should sit directly beside the large smooth belt hole.

guidance.instructionText: Hold both Y-Left carriage halves firmly together and shake the assembly.
guidance.whyItMattersText: Compress the two halves by hand until there is no gap. Shake side-to-side and up-down for 2â€“3 seconds. No tools needed â€” this is a hand-compression test only.

guidance.instructionText: Insert a smooth guide rod through the Y-Left carriage and hold it so the rod is vertical.
guidance.whyItMattersText: The rod should slide or drop through with slight resistance â€” if you have to shake the carriage for the rod to move through, that's correct. Motors pull 20 lbs of belt force; the carriage must not slip too freely.

steps.name: Carriage 1: place bolts and thread nuts
steps.instructionText: Insert 2Ã— M6x18 bolts into the two top holes and 2Ã— M6x30 bolts into the two bottom holes. Thread one M6 nut onto each bolt finger-tight.

steps.name: Carriage 1: hand-tighten â€” prep for drill
steps.instructionText: Thread and finger-tighten all 4 bolts on the Y-Left carriage. Seat each bolt snug by hand before moving to the power drill â€” this prevents cross-threading and lets the drill finish the final torque cleanly.
